messages.author: 7cb65577bc9b60a6
messages.subject: coord_equal and facet_wrap again...
parts:
Hi all,

Following on from a post by JiHo on 21 May 2009, getting isometric
plot (i.e. plots similar to using aspect="iso" in lattice or eqscplot
in MASS) when facet_wrap is being used seems to be fixed in ggplot2
0.8.8 (which I'm using under R version 2.11.1 on Windows XP). But see
the odd behaviour in the last command in the following examples.

# set up example data
d <- data.frame(foo=rep(letters[1:4], each=10))
d$x <- runif(nrow(d),1,10)
d$y <- runif(nrow(d),1,50)

(p1 <- qplot(x, y, data=d))

p1 + facet_grid(~ foo) + coord_equal() # isometric display
p1 + facet_wrap(~ foo, nrow=1) + coord_equal() # ditto
p1 + facet_wrap(~ foo) + coord_equal() # This is what I want except
for...
# ... needing to reverse x & y axes:
qplot(y, x, data=d) + facet_wrap(~foo) + coord_equal(ratio=1) #
bother!

so is this a bug?

many thanks for any insights,

Cheers,

Leon

I think it is. See also my description of it at
http://groups.google.com/group/ggplot2/browse_thread/thread/0e490f32d629eaf9
under the subject "Bug with coord_equal, facet_wrap, and horizontally
stretched axes". As you noted, it only occurs when stretching/
compression is in one direction, but not the other. I didn't figure
out what was the source of the bug then, and have not returned to look
since. Maybe someone else will.

messages.subject: Re: coord_equal and facet_wrap again...

Aaaaahhhh, I see it now. Actually, the difference becomes really obvious with

qplot(y, x, data=d) + facet_grid(~foo) + coord_equal(ratio=1)

using Leon's data. I saw the square plot region in each panel and thought: Problem? Re-running the plot with facet_grid() instead, it seems to produce equal coordinates (as in 10 units of x and 10 units of y produce a square rather than a rectangle), which was Leon's point. Sorry for the misunderstanding - I was looking at the wrong thing.

Cheers,
Dennis
